asks: what does my champ want this game
say: Bully early with three-hit trades and roam for kills off a shoved wave, or stay and farm if their laner punishes every step away.
more: Dirty Fighting makes every third hit from attacks and abilities deal bonus damage and shield you against champions, so short three-hit trades are where you win lane.
Heroic Swing needs terrain to hook onto. Fights next to walls suit you; fights in the open middle of a lane leave you without your escape.
Later you are a short-range marksman who cleans up. Stay on the edge of fights and finish whoever drops low instead of standing in front.
check: Where the nearest wall is before you commit, and whether the wave is shoved before you leave lane.
breaks: If you fall behind in levels from roaming, stop leaving; catch waves until you are even, because your damage needs items like any marksman.

asks: what does my ult do for me
is six a spike on Akshan
say: At six, Comeuppance finishes low targets from range, so chip them first and lock on, or hold it if minions stand between you.
more: Comeuppance hits harder the more health the target is missing, so it is a finisher, not an opener. Trade first, ult second.
The bullets stop on the first champion, minion or structure in the way. A clear line matters more than being close.
It also reaches people running to their tower, which makes roams after six much more likely to end in a kill.
check: Whether a minion, another champion or a tower sits on the line between you and the target.
breaks: If the target can step behind their wave or a tank, do not channel it; walk for a clear angle or keep trading with attacks instead.

asks: how do I trade on Akshan
how do I win lane as Akshan
say: Throw Avengerang through the wave into them, then land two attacks for the shield, or just farm with the boomerang if they out-range you.
more: The boomerang reaches further each time it hits something, so throwing it through minions is how it gets to a laner standing behind them.
Three hits from attacks and abilities trigger Dirty Fighting: bonus damage and a shield. Get the third hit, then back off behind the shield.
Each attack fires a second weaker shot, so two quick attacks after the boomerang finish the three-hit count fast.
check: Their position behind the wave, and whether stepping up for the attacks puts you inside their own combo range.
breaks: Against a champion who wins long fights, do not stay after the third hit; take the shielded trade and walk out, or you give the health back.

when: an ally died in the last 30 seconds
asks: my teammate just died, what now
who do I kill in the fight
what do I do in teamfights as Akshan
say: Whoever killed your teammate is marked: take them down and the ally comes back, or back off if that target is their healthiest tank.
more: Going Rogue marks enemies who kill your allies. If you get the kill on a marked enemy, the allies they killed revive and you get bonus gold.
That turns a lost fight into an even one, so staying alive on the edge until the killer is low is worth more than early damage.
Getting the kill also clears every mark, so pick the marked enemy who killed the most important teammate when you have a choice.
check: Which enemy carries the mark, and how low they are compared with how many of them are still standing.
breaks: If the marked enemy is full health behind their team, chasing them gets you killed too; reset and defend instead of forcing the revive.

asks: when do I leave lane on Akshan
do I roam or stay mid
say: Shove the wave, then roam to the side lane with a wall you can swing off, or stay if your wave won't reach their tower.
more: Heroic Swing circles terrain while firing at the nearest enemy, so a gank that starts beside a wall gives you both the approach and the damage.
Leaving on a shoved wave means their laner has to choose between following you and losing minions under their tower.
After six the roam gets better, because Comeuppance can finish someone who escapes toward their tower.
check: Whether the side lane's enemies are pushed up, and whether the nearest enemy to your swing will be a champion and not a minion.
breaks: If the side lane is shoved into the enemy tower there is nothing to gank; take your own wave or a river ward instead.

asks: what does Brand want to do
say: Burn them down from range and make them fight grouped up, or sit back and hold Sear to stun whoever jumps on you.
more: Every spell sets targets ablaze, and each of your other spells does something extra to a burning target. Order matters more than speed.
You have no dash and no shield. Your safety is the stun from Sear on a burning target, so spending it carelessly leaves you open.
Later you win fights in narrow places where they stand together, because your fire spreads and Pyroclasm bounces between nearby enemies.
check: How close their divers can get to you, and whether enemies are standing together or spread out.
breaks: Against a team that reaches you instantly, stop poking from the front; stand behind your tank and use the stun only on whoever dives.

asks: when am I strong on Brand
when do I use my ult
can I all in at six
say: Six is your kill level: Pyroclasm bounces between enemies standing close, so fight when they bunch, or hold it if the target is alone and far.
more: Pyroclasm bounces up to five times off you and nearby enemies, and the bounces try to stack your burn on champions.
Two enemies standing together, or one enemy close to you, keep the fire bouncing. One enemy far away with nothing nearby gets very little.
Bot lane at six is the classic moment: both of them are usually near each other and near minions.
check: How many targets are close enough together for the bounces, and whether you would have to walk into them to keep it going.
breaks: If bouncing off yourself means standing in their damage, do not ult for it; poke with Pillar of Flame and wait for them to group.

asks: how do I trade as Brand
how do I land the stun
what order do I use my spells
say: Open with Conflagration so Sear stuns, then Pillar of Flame on the stunned target, or lead with Pillar from range if walking up isn't safe.
more: Sear only stuns a target that is already ablaze, so any other spell has to land first. Conflagration is the reliable one because it is targeted.
Pillar of Flame deals 25 percent more to burning targets, so it hits hardest as the last spell, on someone who cannot move.
Conflagration spreads further from a burning target, so casting it on a burning minion next to them is a way to light them without walking closer.
check: Whether minions block the path of Sear, and how far you must step forward to reach them with Conflagration.
breaks: If the stun misses you have nothing to stop them walking at you; back off until Sear is ready again instead of finishing the combo.

asks: how do I clear on Brand
do I gank early or farm
where do I go first as Brand jungle
say: Your fire spreads through camps, so full clear both sides to level four, or stop at three camps and gank a lane that's pushed toward you.
more: Conflagration spreads and Pillar of Flame hits an area, so camps with several monsters die quickly. Killing burning monsters gives mana back.
You have no dash, and your stun needs another spell to land first. Early ganks only work when the enemy is far from their tower.
A full clear finishes around level four near the 2:55 crab spawn, which lets you arrive at river with every spell available.
check: Your health after the single big monsters, and whether a laner near you has the enemy pushed up to your tower.
breaks: If their jungler is an early fighter and walks into your jungle, do not duel him; give the camp, take the far side and call your laners.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Brand
where do I stand in fights
say: Stay behind your front line and throw Pyroclasm once they bunch up, or keep Sear's stun for a diver if one reaches you first.
more: Your damage comes from spreading fire across several people. A fight in a jungle corridor or at a pit entrance does that for you.
Pyroclasm prioritizes stacking the burn on champions, so casting it into the middle of a clump is better than picking the perfect target.
You are the easiest kill on your team. Arriving a second late, after their engage is used, usually deals more than arriving first.
check: Where their divers and hooks are, and whether the enemies are grouped or fanned out when the fight starts.
breaks: If they spread wide and send one diver at you, forget the big ult; stun the diver, burn him with your team and reset.

say: Farm quietly to six, then kill squishy targets from stealth all game, or cover a lane early only when the kill is already set up.
more: Before six you are a jungler without stealth and without hard crowd control on demand. After six, Demon Shade camouflages you out of combat.
Your threat is one target at a time. The game you want is isolated carries walking between lanes, not five against five front to back.
Demon Shade also heals you when you are low and out of combat, so you can reset between attempts without going home every time.
check: Which enemies are squishy enough to kill alone, and whether they are walking around without teammates.
breaks: If their team groups tightly with tanks in front, stop hunting; stay near your carry and charm whoever dives them instead.

asks: how do I path on Evelynn
should I farm or gank early as Eve
say: No stealth before six, so full clear both sides for level four, or gank only a lane that's already shoved up to your tower.
more: A full clear is about level four. Six is the level that changes your game, so every skipped camp pushes your real start later.
Demon Shade heals you when you are low and out of combat, so walking between camps tops you up and keeps the clear going.
Early ganks are visible the whole way in. They work when the enemy is far up the lane and your laner can hold them.
check: Your health after each big monster, and how far up the lane the enemy laner is standing before you walk over.
breaks: If their jungler invades you early, do not fight him alone; give the camp, cross to the other side and keep the level race going.

asks: how do I get six faster
do I fight for crab as Eve
say: Chain camps without stopping and take a crab on the way to speed up six, or give the crab if their jungler is a level up.
more: Both crabs spawn at 2:55 and the first full clear ends about level four, so the crab is a bonus on the way, not a fight to die for.
Small camps return about two and a quarter minutes after you kill them. Clearing in the same order each time means one is always coming back.
Reaching six before their jungler turns the next river meeting into your fight, because you arrive unseen.
check: Whether their jungler is at the crab and which of your laners can move first.
breaks: If their jungler is stronger early and his laners are pushed up, skip the crab entirely and take your next camp; dying there delays six most.

asks: what changes at six for Evelynn
say: Six gives you stealth and Last Caress, so start ganking lanes from behind, or keep farming if no lane has a squishy target to kill.
more: Camouflage out of combat means lanes cannot see you walking in the way they see other junglers. The gank starts from where you choose.
Last Caress makes you untargetable for a moment and throws you a long way back, so it is both your finishing hit and your way out.
Each kill on a carry here stretches your lead into the next objective, because that player arrives late and weaker.
check: Whether the lane has control wards down, and whether the target has teammates close enough to answer.
breaks: If Last Caress is used, you have no exit. Do not go deep again until it is back; farm a camp or two instead.

asks: how do I gank as Evelynn
how do I use the charm
what's my gank combo on Eve
say: Curse them with Allure while hidden and wait out the delay so your first hit charms, or skip the wait if they're already low.
more: Allure needs a delay before your next attack or spell charms. Hitting early wastes it, so the patience is the whole gank.
The charm also cuts their magic resist, which is why your follow-up hits so hard right after it lands.
Whiplash gives you a burst of move speed after it hits, which helps you stay on them or get out.
check: Whether they noticed the curse and are already walking away, and how far they are from their tower.
breaks: If they run the moment Allure appears, do not chase under tower; the lane still lost pressure, so take that and try another lane.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Eve
where do I wait in fights
say: Wait hidden on the side for a squishy carry, kill them and Last Caress out, or stay with your own carry and charm whoever dives.
more: You are not the one who starts the fight. Let the front lines meet, then arrive from an angle where their back line is not looking.
Last Caress hits the area in front of you, so more than one low enemy in front is the best moment for it.
If no carry is reachable, a charm on their diver next to your own carry is still a real contribution.
check: Where their carries stand relative to their tanks, and whether they have placed control wards near the fight.
breaks: If they reveal you before the fight, do not force the flank; walk back to your team and play as a second line of damage.

say: You win by range: clear waves and poke from far back with Disaster spells, or keep a Torment spell ready if they can jump you.
more: Each basic ability opens a set of three spells: Disaster for damage, Serenity for utility, Torment for crowd control. You pick the tool for the moment.
You have no dash. Your safety is distance and the control spell you saved, so position first and cast second.
Later, you are the one who softens a team before an objective and then controls the space where the fight happens.
check: Which of their champions can close the gap on you, and how far you are from them.
breaks: If they dive you every time, stop leading with damage; stand further back and open with a Torment spell on whoever comes.

asks: what do I do with my ult
is six a spike on Hwei
how do I use Spiraling Despair
say: At six, land a Torment spell first and then stick Spiraling Despair on them, or throw it into a grouped team before an objective fight.
more: Spiraling Despair attaches to the first champion it hits and grows into an area that slows and damages everyone near them.
On one target it sets up your other spells because they are slowed. On a clump it splits their team or makes them walk out of the fight.
It counts as a damaging spell, so it also helps finish your signature when paired with another hit.
check: Whether a tank is standing in front to absorb it, and how tightly their team is grouped.
breaks: If their front line will body-block it, do not open with it; wait until the fight starts and their carries step forward.

asks: how do I trade on Hwei
how do I poke as Hwei
what's the Hwei combo in lane
how do I get my passive off
say: Land one damaging spell, then a second right away to finish your signature under them, or just clear the wave if the first one misses.
more: The first damaging spell primes a champion. A second damaging spell completes the signature and leaves it beneath them for extra damage.
That means two spells on one target is worth much more than one spell on each of two targets.
Using a Torment spell first makes the second hit far easier, but it leaves you without that control if their jungler arrives.
check: Whether the enemy is primed, and where their jungler could be before you spend your control spell.
breaks: If you are low on mana, stop fishing for the second spell; use Disaster spells on the wave only and trade again after you recall.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Hwei
which spells do I use in fights
say: Stay at max range, control the choke with Torment spells and hit whoever's closest, or use Serenity spells on your team if they dive.
more: You deal the most when the fight stays in one place. Control spells on the entrance to a pit or jungle path keep it there.
Hitting the nearest target twice finishes your signature. Chasing their back line through the front line gets you caught.
Serenity is your utility set. When your team is the one being jumped on, helping them live is often worth more than another damage spell.
check: Who is diving your team, and whether you have a control spell still available.
breaks: If their assassin is alive and unseen, hold your Torment spell and stand next to a teammate instead of casting everything forward.

asks: what do I do mid game on Hwei
where should I be as Hwei
say: Clear mid fast and get to the next objective first to poke before it starts, or catch a side wave if nothing spawns soon.
more: Your range lets you clear a wave without walking into it, so you can leave mid before their laner does.
Arriving first means the enemy walks into your spells on the way in. Half a health bar missing before the fight is your contribution.
Dragon returns five minutes after a kill and baron is in the top pit from 20:00, so use those timers to decide which side to shove toward.
check: Which objective is up next and whether your team has vision on the way there.
breaks: If your team is not coming, do not poke alone at the pit; take the side wave and give the objective instead of dying for it.

say: Farm camps hard and use Requiem whenever a fight breaks out anywhere, or walk to a gank only if that lane brings its own stun.
more: Requiem damages every enemy champion wherever they are after a three second channel. You help lanes without leaving your jungle.
Your own crowd control is only a slow from Wall of Pain, so ganks that rely on you to hold someone rarely work.
You scale with gold and levels. Ten minutes of clean farming plus a few Requiem assists is a better game than forced early plays.
check: Enemy health bars in fights across the map, since the coach cannot see them.
breaks: If their jungler keeps taking your camps, stop farming alone; ward your entrances and clear next to whichever of your lanes is strongest.

asks: how do I clear as Karthus
should I gank early on Karthus
say: Full clear both sides for level four, that's your job early, or cut it to three camps if their jungler invades and you can't fight.
more: Lay Waste hits harder on an isolated enemy, so single big monsters and the last monster left in a camp die faster than you expect.
Defile burns mana quickly while it is on but gives mana back for each kill. Turn it on for groups, off for single monsters.
Finishing near level four around the 2:55 crab spawn is on schedule. You are farming toward six, not looking for a fight at the crab.
check: Your mana after each camp, and whether their jungler has shown up near your side.
breaks: If you are low on health and mana after the first side, recall before the second; a slow full clear beats dying to an invade.

asks: I'm six on Karthus now what
say: At six, watch your lanes and channel Requiem from safety to finish low enemies, or save it for the next objective fight if nobody's low.
more: Requiem channels for three seconds and then hits every enemy champion. Use it when someone is low and running, not when the fight is starting.
Because it hits everyone, a fight at dragon or grubs with several hurt enemies is worth more than one kill in a side lane.
The three seconds are the risk. Being hit out of the channel wastes it, so step out of sight first.
check: How low the enemies are, and whether anyone can reach and interrupt you during the channel.
breaks: If the low target has a heal or shield nearby, the kill will not come; keep Requiem for the objective fight where it hits five.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Karthus
where do I stand on Karthus
is it ok to die in fights
say: Walk into the middle with Defile on and keep casting after you die, or stay back and Requiem late if your team needs you alive.
more: Death Defied lets you keep casting spells as a spirit after dying, so dying in the centre of their team still deals your damage.
Wall of Pain across their path slows them and lowers their magic resist, which makes your damage and your team's magic damage hit harder.
Lay Waste hits harder on someone standing alone, so the carry who steps away from the group is your best target.
check: Whether Requiem is ready, and whether dying here loses your team the objective after the fight.
breaks: If the fight is for baron or soul and smite matters, do not walk in to die; stay alive behind your team until the objective is secured.

asks: do I go top or keep farming
say: Gank only where your laner can hold them still, with Wall of Pain behind them, or keep farming and answer their fights with Requiem.
more: Wall of Pain slows anyone who walks through it. Placed between the enemy and their tower, it buys time for your laner's stun to land.
Lay Waste has a delay, so it rarely hits a moving target unless someone else stops them first.
Every gank costs camps. Since Requiem reaches all lanes anyway after six, the bar for walking over should be high.
check: Whether that laner's crowd control is ready and how far the enemy stands from their tower.
breaks: If the lane has no way to hold the enemy, skip it; take the camps on that side and hover so they play scared of you anyway.

say: Shove waves with Ice Shard and look to lock one person down for your team, or play safe and farm if you can't reach them.
more: You are a mage who starts fights. Glacial Path gets you in, Ring of Frost roots everyone around you, and Frozen Tomb stuns one target.
Your value is the pick, not the damage chart. One frozen carry before an objective usually decides it.
Your team has to be near enough to follow. Going in alone only works when Frozen Tomb on yourself can keep you alive.
check: Whether teammates are close enough to follow your engage, and where the enemy carry stands.
breaks: If your team is behind and cannot follow, stop engaging; hold your root and stun for whoever dives your carry.

asks: what do I do at six on Liss
when do I use Frozen Tomb
is six a spike for Lissandra
say: Six gives Frozen Tomb two jobs: freeze their laner when your jungler arrives, or cast it on yourself to survive when they dive you.
more: On an enemy it is a stun long enough for a jungler to arrive and land everything. That makes mid very gankable for your side.
On yourself you become untargetable and invulnerable and heal, which ruins an assassin's all-in or a tower dive.
An enemy who dies near you becomes a Frozen Thrall that slows and then damages those nearby, so kills in a group chain into more.
check: Where your jungler is, and whether their laner is the kind who will jump on you.
breaks: If you use it aggressively and miss the kill, you have no safety for a while; play back from the wave until it returns.

asks: how do I trade on Lissandra
how do I poke as Liss
when do I go in for a trade
how do I hit Q on them
say: Throw Ice Shard through a minion so the shards hit them behind the wave, or walk up for Ring of Frost only with your claw ready.
more: Ice Shard shatters on the first enemy and the shards pass through to others behind for the same damage. Minions extend your poke.
Ring of Frost only roots enemies near you, so using it means standing in their range. Glacial Path is how you leave afterwards.
Poking this way pushes the wave too, which fits your plan: a shoved wave lets you move to river first.
check: Where they stand relative to their minions, and whether your claw is available before you step forward.
breaks: If pushing the wave leaves you far up with no escape, last-hit instead and save the poke for when the wave is near your side.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Liss
who do I ult in fights
when do I go in on Lissandra
say: Claw in, root the group with Ring of Frost and freeze their carry, or stay back and tomb whoever dives your own carry instead.
more: Going in works when your team is right behind you and their carries are close together. The root holds them for your team's damage.
After the root you are surrounded, so decide before you go whether Frozen Tomb is for their carry or for yourself.
Staying back is the better use when their threat is a diver: root them near your carry and stun them in place.
check: How grouped their team is, and whether your team is in range to follow within a second or two.
breaks: If their team is spread out, a deep engage catches one person and kills you; play the peel role and wait for a tighter fight.

when: their mid laner is an assassin
asks: how do I lane against an assassin as Liss
how do I not die to this assassin
what do I do when they jump on me
say: Against an assassin, keep Ring of Frost for the moment they jump you, or after six tomb yourself and wait out their burst.
more: Assassins have to come to you, and you root everything around you. If the root is available when they arrive, the trade is yours.
Use Ice Shard for the wave and poke, and keep the root and the claw unspent whenever they are close enough to go.
This is one of the lanes where simply not dying wins: they fall off in grouped fights and you get stronger in them.
check: Whether their level six came before yours, and whether they have Ignite.
breaks: If you already used the root on the wave, back off to your tower until it returns; do not stand in their range without it.

asks: can I gank bot as Liss
say: After six, shove and walk to a side lane, claw in and freeze one target, or stay mid if your wave is stuck in the middle.
more: A roaming Lissandra brings a stun and a root, which is more lockdown than most junglers have. One landed stun is usually a kill.
Bot lane has two targets close together, so Ring of Frost often roots both and a kill there can turn into a dragon.
Leaving on a shoved wave costs you nothing; leaving on a wave in the middle gives their laner free minions and tower damage.
check: How far up the side-lane enemies are, and where their mid laner goes when you leave.
breaks: If the side lane is already pushed to the enemy tower, do not dive without your jungler; drop a ward in river and go back mid.

say: Shove with your pack, then hunt one squishy target at a time, or keep farming until six if they stay close to their tower.
more: Your packmates attack whatever you attack or hit with abilities, so waves and camps fall quickly and you can leave lane early.
You are simple and direct: daggers, dash, kill. That works on isolated carries and badly into a team standing together.
From six, Hounds' Pursuit lets you dash at a champion and go again after a takedown, so fights you start should be ones you can finish.
check: How many packmates are alive with you, and whether your target has teammates nearby.
breaks: If they group early and you cannot find anyone alone, stop forcing picks; push a side wave so someone has to come to you.

asks: I'm six now what on Naafiri
how do I use my ult
can I all in at six
say: At six, Hounds' Pursuit lets you dash onto a champion from range, so pick a low or lonely target, or wait if their teammates are near.
more: You and your pack dash at the champion together. A takedown reveals nearby enemies and lets you cast it again, and the second cast shields you.
So the first kill decides the fight: get it and you have a second dash and a shield to take another target or leave.
The Call of the Pack adds more packmates and makes you untargetable for a moment, which is how you dodge the one spell that would stop you.
check: Whether the first target is really killable, and which enemy spell you need to dodge.
breaks: If you do not get the takedown there is no recast and no shield; do not start on a tank or a full-health target near their tower.

asks: how do I clear on Naafiri
farm or gank early on Naafiri
where do I path as Naafiri
say: Your pack adds damage on every camp, so full clear to level four then gank, or gank at three if a lane near you is low.
more: Packmates leap onto the first monster your daggers hit, and Eviscerate calls them back and fully heals them. Use it to keep the pack alive.
The clear is healthy enough that either plan works. A full clear ends about level four as both crabs spawn at 2:55.
Before six your gank is a dash and a bleed with no stun, so it needs a lane that can hold the enemy or one who is already hurt.
check: How many packmates you still have, and the health of the enemy laner nearest your third camp.
breaks: If an early gank burns nothing and gets nothing, go straight back to camps; do not wait in a bush while your jungle sits full.

asks: how do I trade on Naafiri
how do I win lane as Naafiri
say: Land the first dagger for the bleed and the second for bonus damage, then dash in, or just poke with daggers if they win up close.
more: Darkin Daggers can be thrown twice. The first applies a bleed; a dagger that hits an already bleeding target deals bonus damage instead.
Packmates leap at the first champion the dagger hits, so a landed dagger also sends the pack onto them.
Eviscerate is a dash that damages around you and heals the pack. Used to go in, it is not there to get out.
check: Whether your packmates are alive, and whether their jungler could be near when you dash forward.
breaks: If their laner clears your pack with area spells, trade only after that spell is used on the wave, or wait for the pack to return.

when: their mid laner is a mage
asks: how do I play against a mage as Naafiri
what do I do when my pack dies
say: If their spells keep hitting your pack, pull it back with Eviscerate to heal it, or trade right after they spend spells on the wave.
more: Much of your damage is the pack. A mage who hits it with area spells every wave is taking your trades away before they start.
Eviscerate recalls the packmates and fully heals them, so one well-timed dash resets the pack to full.
At six the lane changes: Hounds' Pursuit gets you onto a mage directly, and most mages have no answer once you are on top of them.
check: How many packmates are left and how hurt they are, and which enemy spell was just used.
breaks: If you cannot keep the pack alive at all, give up lane kills; farm with daggers from range and look for roams after six.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Naafiri
say: Wait until their stuns are used, then Hounds' Pursuit onto a carry, or stay out and clean up low targets to earn the recast.
more: You need one takedown to unlock the second dash and its shield. Entering late on a hurt carry gets that far more often than entering first.
The Call of the Pack makes you untargetable briefly. Save it for the spell that would lock you down as you arrive.
If the carry is unreachable, any low target is fine. The recast then carries you to the back line.
check: Which of their crowd control spells have been used, and who on their team is already low.
breaks: If their team stays together with every stun available, do not dive; threaten from the side so their carry has to stand further back.

say: Pull one target with Bone Skewer and finish them with your team, or roam mid when your bot wave is pushed to their tower.
more: You are a support who gets kills. Death From Below executes low enemies and gives extra gold to an ally who assists, so your kills still feed your team.
You cannot gain extra maximum health; it becomes attack damage instead. You are never a front line, at any stage.
Your best game is fast and spread across the map: bot kill, mid roam, river fight. Long grouped games are harder for you.
check: Whether your lane partner can follow up on a hook, and where the enemy support is standing.
breaks: If your lane partner needs protecting more than kills, stop roaming; stay and use your pull and stun to peel for them.

asks: what do I do at six on Pyke
is six a spike for Pyke
say: At six, start fights where someone can get low: Death From Below executes and resets, or hold it if nobody is close to dying.
more: Death From Below executes enemies below a health threshold and can be cast again right after an execute, so one low enemy can turn into several.
An ally who assists gets additional gold from the execute. A fight near teammates is worth more than a solo pick.
This is why bot lane fights at six favor you: any trade that leaves them low ends with your ult.
check: The execute indicator on enemy health bars, which the coach cannot see.
breaks: If you cast it on someone above the execute line you get no reset; wait for the indicator instead of pressing it to start the fight.

asks: how do I trade on Pyke
how do I lane as Pyke
how do I heal back up
say: Trade short, then step out of their sight to heal back what champions dealt, or stop trading if they can keep you in view.
more: Gift of the Drowned Ones regenerates damage you recently took from champions while enemies cannot see you. Bushes and Ghostwater Dive both work.
Bone Skewer is two spells: a quick stab up close or a held pull at range. Pull when your partner can hit them, stab when they walk at you.
Phantom Undertow dashes you forward and stuns anyone the returning phantom passes through, so dash through them, not at them.
check: Whether the bush you plan to hide in is warded, and whether your partner is in range to follow a pull.
breaks: If they ward your bushes, the heal stops working; shorten trades, clear the ward, or hook only when a kill is possible.

say: When your wave is crashing, dive into Ghostwater and roam mid for a hook, or stay if your partner would be left alone under pressure.
more: Ghostwater Dive camouflages you and gives a large burst of move speed that fades, so you cover the distance to mid quickly and unseen.
A roam that starts as the wave reaches their tower costs your partner very little, because the enemy has to clear minions first.
Mid is the short trip. A kill or a burned Flash there also helps the next dragon or grub fight, since mid moves first.
check: Whether the bot wave is really going into their tower, and how far up the enemy mid laner stands.
breaks: If the roam finds nothing in a few seconds, come straight back; a long absence loses your partner the lane.

when: you have more kills than deaths
asks: am I stealing kills as Pyke
what do I do with all this gold
say: Finish kills with your ult when an ally helped, since they get gold too, or leave the kill to your carry if it isn't ready.
more: Death From Below grants extra gold to an assisting ally, so an execute usually pays your team more than a normal last hit does.
Your own gold becomes attack damage, never health. A fed Pyke hits hard but dies as fast as before, so play picks, not front-line fights.
Use the lead quickly: catch someone before each objective so your team starts it with a numbers advantage.
check: Whether an ally actually damaged the target, and whether your ult is available.
breaks: If the game goes long and they group behind tanks, your lead fades; stay near your carry and use your pull and stun defensively.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Pyke
where do I stand late game on Pyke
how do I not die instantly
say: Stay on the edge until someone drops low, then execute and chain resets, or use your pull and stun to protect your carry.
more: You cannot build health, so walking in first is a death with nothing gained. Let someone else start the fight.
A pull on a carry who steps too far forward is the best opening you can offer. Miss it and you still have the stun to disengage.
Once one execute lands the reset lets you look for the next low target straight away.
check: Enemy health bars for the execute indicator, and where their burst damage is pointed.
breaks: If nobody on their team is getting low, do not dive for it; peel with Phantom Undertow and wait for your team's damage.

say: You're the engage: set up kills for your lanes and start objective fights, or stand by your carry and stun divers if you're behind.
more: Arctic Assault knocks up, Permafrost stuns a target with full Frost, and Glacial Prison stuns from range. Your kit is three ways to stop someone.
You do not carry with damage. Your gold matters less than whether your laners are ahead, so play for their lanes.
Frost Armor gives you armor, magic resist and slow immunity after being out of combat, so you are toughest in the first seconds of a fight.
check: Which of your laners can deal damage when you stun someone, and whether their wave lets you reach the enemy.
breaks: If all your lanes are losing, stop ganking into them; farm, protect the strongest teammate and fight only at objectives.

asks: how do I clear on Sejuani
do I gank early or full clear
where do I start as Sejuani
say: Full clear to level four, Frost Armor keeps you healthy between camps, or gank at three if a lane has the enemy pushed up.
more: Frost Armor returns after you are out of combat for a moment, so each camp starts with extra armor and magic resist.
Winter's Wrath swings twice in an area and is your main clearing tool. Arctic Assault helps you move between camps.
At three you already have knock-up, Frost and stun, so an early gank is real. The cost is arriving at the 2:55 crabs a level behind.
check: Your health, and how far the enemy laner near your third camp is from their tower.
breaks: If their jungler is a strong early duelist, do not meet him alone at crab; finish your camps and arrive with a laner.

asks: how do I gank on Sejuani
how do I land the stun
say: Charge in with Arctic Assault, swing Winter's Wrath for Frost, then Permafrost to stun, or walk up and keep the charge for their dash.
more: Permafrost only works on a champion with maximum Frost stacks. Winter's Wrath applies Frost, so the swing has to land before the stun.
Arctic Assault stops on the first champion it hits. Aim it at the target you want, not through their support or a second enemy.
Pick lanes where your laner has damage ready. Two stops in a row with nobody hitting the target is a wasted trip.
check: Whether the enemy still has a dash or Flash, and whether your laner is healthy enough to follow.
breaks: If the lane is pushed to the enemy tower, do not force it; take the camps on that side and come back when the wave turns.

asks: what do I do at six on Sejuani
when do I use my ult
how do I use Glacial Prison
say: Six gives you a ranged stun, so gank a lane that was too far to reach before, or keep it for the next objective fight.
more: Glacial Prison stuns the first champion it hits and leaves a storm that slows the others. It starts a fight from outside their reach.
In a lane it removes the need to get close first: bola, then charge, then Frost and stun. That is a very long lockdown.
At an objective it catches whoever walks in first. With grubs from 8:00 and dragons on a five minute timer, having it ready there matters.
check: Whether a tank is standing in front to absorb the bola, and which objective comes next.
breaks: If their front line blocks it, throw it only after the fight has started and the carry is exposed, or use it to stop a diver.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Sej
when do I go in on Sejuani
say: Start the fight with Glacial Prison on whoever steps forward and charge in, or hold everything to stun divers if your carry is the win condition.
more: Engaging first works when your team has more damage ready than theirs. The stun plus storm slow gives them a clear target.
Peeling works when one fed teammate is doing the work. A knock-up and a stun on the diver often keeps that teammate alive through the fight.
Either way, land Winter's Wrath on as many as possible so Permafrost is available on the one who matters.
check: Who the strongest player on each team is, and whether your team is close enough to follow an engage.
breaks: If your team is split or late to the fight, do not engage alone; stall with slows and wait for them to arrive.

when: you are 2 or more levels behind their jungler
asks: I'm behind on Sejuani what do I do
how do I come back as Sej
say: Your stuns don't need gold, so shadow your strongest laner and fight with them, or trade the opposite objective if you can't contest.
more: A knock-up and two stuns are worth the same at any item count. What you lose behind is the ability to survive alone.
So stop meeting their jungler one on one. Clear the camps next to your best lane and be there when they fight.
If they start dragon, taking herald or grubs on the other side keeps the game even instead of losing a fight and the objective.
check: Which of your laners is ahead, and which objective their jungler is moving toward.
breaks: If there is nothing to trade on the other side, give the objective and catch waves and camps; dying for it makes the gap bigger.

say: Poke and collect Soul Fragments early, then walk into grouped fights and drain, or stay behind your front line if they kite you.
more: Ravenous Flock heals you from Soul Fragments and permanently raises your maximum health, so you grow tankier the longer the game goes.
Demonic Ascension drains health from nearby enemies. You want long fights in tight spaces with several enemies around you.
You are slow and have no dash. Nevermove's root and pull is how you start, and a missed one means you wait.
check: Whether their team can keep away from you, and how many enemies would be near you if you walk in.
breaks: Against long-range teams that never let you get close, stop walking forward; peel for your carry and root whoever comes to you.

asks: what do I do at six on Swain
say: At six you win extended two-on-two fights: root, pull, then Demonic Ascension, or wait for your jungler if they can just walk away.
more: Demonic Ascension drains nearby enemy champions, minions and monsters, so fighting inside a wave heals you more.
Nevermove comes back faster while you are transformed, so one landed root often leads to a second.
Demonflare ends it with a blast that damages and slows. Use it when they try to leave, not the instant it is available.
check: Whether enemies will stay within the drain, and how big the minion wave around you is.
breaks: If they have dashes to leave the drain at once, do not ult first; land Nevermove, and only transform once they are pulled in.

asks: how do I trade on Swain
how do I land the root
how do I lane as Swain
say: Throw Nevermove past them so it roots on the way back, pull them in and hit Death's Hand, or poke with Vision of Empire from range.
more: Nevermove roots on its return trip, not on the way out. Aim so the far end is behind them, then they must dodge twice.
Death's Hand fires several bolts and hurts more for each one that hits, so it is strongest point blank on a pulled target.
Vision of Empire damages, slows and reveals from a distance, and each champion hit gives a Soul Fragment. It is your safe poke.
check: Whether minions or their support stand in the way, and whether pulling them in also pulls you into their partner's damage.
breaks: If the root misses, do not walk up anyway; you have nothing to hold them, so back off until it is ready again.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Swain
where do I stand on Swain
when do I ult in a fight
say: Walk in beside your front line, transform once several enemies are near and keep pulling, or guard your carry if they have the range.
more: The drain hits everyone nearby, so your healing and damage both scale with how many enemies stand around you.
A root that catches two and pulls them into your team is often the fight. Throw it down the corridor they are walking through.
Go in second, not first. A tank ahead of you takes the opening burst and you arrive while their spells are already spent.
check: How many enemies are within reach, and whether their heavy crowd control has been used.
breaks: If they focus you first and you are dropping fast, walk back out through your team; your drain is wasted if you die at the start.

asks: how do I get tanky on Swain
what's my long game on Swain
say: Collect Soul Fragments all game: pull champions with Nevermove and tag them with Vision of Empire, or just farm safely if they out-range you.
more: Each Soul Fragment heals you and permanently adds maximum health. Landing spells on champions is how they appear.
It adds up slowly, so a quiet lane with steady fragments is fine. You do not need kills early to matter at twenty-five minutes.
Vision of Empire gives a fragment for each champion it hits and reveals them, so casting it into a fight you are walking toward helps twice.
check: How often your spells are landing on champions, and whether you are giving up minions to chase fragments.
breaks: If chasing fragments costs you health and waves, stop; farm first, and take fragments only when the spell is free to cast.

say: Clear fast, run at people with Blazing Stampede and stun them, or stay on camps and out-farm their jungler if lanes aren't gankable.
more: You swap between four stances: claws for single targets, mantle to shield and heal, stampede to run and stun, storm for area damage and slows.
Recasting a stance empowers it. Choosing which one gets the empowered cast is most of the skill on this champion.
You have no dash and no ranged spell. Everything you do starts with walking up to someone, so move speed and angles matter.
check: Whether the enemy can keep away from you with dashes or slows, since you only threaten what you can reach.
breaks: If they kite you all game, stop chasing carries; stand in front of your own carry and stun whoever comes in.

asks: how do I clear on Udyr
farm or gank early on Udyr
say: Storm for group camps, claws for single monsters, and full clear to level four, or gank at three since Stampede's stun already works.
more: Wingborne Storm damages everything around you, so it is the stance for camps with several monsters. Wilding Claw is for a single big one.
Iron Mantle shields you and heals on your next two attacks, so casting it when you dip keeps you healthy between camps.
Your clear is quick and safe, so the default is full clear into the 2:55 crabs. Farming well is a real plan on this champion.
check: Your health and mana after each side of the jungle, and whether a lane next to your third camp is pushed toward you.
breaks: If you run low on mana from swapping stances too often, slow down and recall after the clear instead of walking to crab empty.

asks: how do I gank on Udyr
which lane do I gank as Udyr
say: Come from behind with Blazing Stampede and stun with your first hit, or skip lanes where they can dash away and farm instead.
more: Blazing Stampede gives move speed and makes your first attack on each target stun them. You have to reach them on foot first.
That means the angle matters more than for most junglers. Coming from behind the enemy, between them and their tower, is the gank.
The empowered recast gives more speed and makes you immune to immobilizing effects for a couple of seconds, so you can run through a root.
check: Whether the enemy has a dash or Flash, and whether the wave position lets you get behind them.
breaks: If they see you early and walk away, do not chase to the tower; you forced them off the wave, so go back to camps.

say: You have no ultimate to wait for, so fight on level leads and each finished item, or keep farming if you're behind in both.
more: Udyr has four basic abilities and an empowered recast, not a level six ultimate. Your strength rises smoothly with ranks and items.
That makes early levels good for you: against a jungler who is waiting for six, the minutes before it are your window.
Compare levels before each river fight. A level up with full health is your green light; even levels against a champion with an ultimate is not.
check: Your level against their jungler's, which the coach can read out, and your health before the fight.
breaks: Once their jungler has an ultimate and you are even, stop looking for one-on-ones; fight with a laner or trade camps.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Udyr
say: Run in with Stampede and stun each target once with the storm on, or stay by your carry and stun whoever dives them.
more: Stampede's stun works on your first attack against each target, so hitting several different enemies spreads short stuns across their team.
Wingborne Storm slows and damages everyone near you. Empowered, it tracks enemies, so it keeps working while you chase.
Iron Mantle is your survival. Saving the empowered cast for it in a big fight often keeps you alive long enough to matter.
check: Whether you can actually reach their carries, and which stance still has its empowered cast.
breaks: If their back line has dashes and you cannot reach it, do not run past their tanks; fight the front line with your team.

when: their jungler just took part in a kill in a lane
asks: can I take their camps as Udyr
their jungler showed, what do I do
say: He just showed in a lane, so take a camp on his far side and leave with Stampede, or farm your own if lanes can't help.
more: Your clear is fast and Stampede gets you out quickly, so stealing one camp while he is busy costs little time.
Small camps come back about two and a quarter minutes later. Taking one from him puts his next clear behind yours.
Over several clears this is how a farming jungler gets a level lead without ever fighting.
check: Which lane the kill happened in, so you enter on the opposite side, and whether their nearby laners are pushed up.
breaks: If he died or recalled, he may respawn onto his own camps; take one camp only and leave, do not go for a second.

say: Farm safely, lay feathers and punish anyone who walks through them, or play aggressive if your support can hold a target in place.
more: After an ability your attacks hit everything in a line and leave feathers. Bladecaller pulls them back, damaging and rooting.
So you are a marksman who is dangerous to run at. Divers have to cross your feathers to reach you.
Featherstorm makes you untargetable for a moment, which is unusual safety for a carry. It lets you stand a little closer in fights.
check: Where your feathers are lying on the ground, and which direction the enemy would have to walk to reach you.
breaks: Against long-range poke that never walks at you, feathers do little; farm with your line attacks and wait for item power.

asks: what do I do at six on Xayah
say: Six gives you Featherstorm to dodge their engage and drop feathers for a root, or use it aggressively if they've already spent their spells.
more: Featherstorm lifts you untargetable and throws a fan of daggers that leave feathers. Bladecaller right after pulls them all back through the enemy.
Defensively it erases an all-in: the hook or the burst lands on nothing and they are now standing in your feathers.
Your damage also climbs with each finished item, like any marksman. Deadly Plumage's attack speed gets better the more damage you have.
check: Which enemy spell you most need to dodge, and whether they are close enough for the feathers to pass through them.
breaks: If you use it to start a fight and they still have their engage, you have no answer left; keep it until theirs is gone.

asks: how do I trade on Xayah
what's the Xayah combo in lane
say: Throw Double Daggers past them, attack once or twice, then Bladecaller the feathers back through them, or just last-hit if they stay far.
more: Double Daggers drops feathers behind where they land. Feathers have to travel through an enemy on the way back to hit them.
Bladecaller roots when enough feathers pass through one target, so stacking a few in a line behind them before recalling is the goal.
Deadly Plumage adds attack speed and damage, and gives move speed when you attack a champion. Use it when you commit to the trade.
check: Whether the feathers are on the far side of the enemy from you, and how many there are.
breaks: If they sidestep the line, do not call the feathers back for nothing; keep them down as a threat or use them on the wave.

asks: how do I push the wave on Xayah
how do I clear waves fast
say: Cast an ability, then attack down the line of minions to shove fast and recall, or last-hit only if their jungler hasn't shown.
more: Clean Cuts makes your attacks after an ability hit every target along their path. A lined-up wave takes damage all at once.
Bladecaller pulls the feathers back through the wave too, so it finishes the minions you already hit.
A fast shove before a recall means the wave reaches their tower and you lose little while buying.
check: Whether the minions are lined up, and how long since their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If you used Bladecaller on the wave, you have no root for a gank; shove only when you can leave right after.

when: their support is an engage champion
asks: how do I lane against engage as Xayah
what do I do against hook supports
say: Against engage, keep feathers between you and them and root whoever comes in, or after six leap with Featherstorm as they commit.
more: An engage support has to walk or dash toward you. If your feathers are already lying on that path, their engage ends in your root.
So attack the wave from a spot where the feathers fall in front of you, toward them, not off to the side.
After six you have two answers, the root and the untargetable leap. Using one and keeping the other is usually enough.
check: Where your feathers are before they engage, and whether your own support can protect you.
breaks: If you have no feathers down, you are a normal marksman with no escape; stand behind minions and further back until you do.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Xayah
when do I ult in fights
where do I stand on Xayah
say: Hit the nearest enemy from behind your front line and root divers with feathers, or hold Featherstorm for their one big engage spell.
more: Your attacks pierce in a line after abilities, so shooting the tank in front still damages and drops feathers under whoever stands behind.
Feathers collect quickly in a fight. When a diver reaches you they have usually crossed several, so Bladecaller stops them.
Featherstorm is worth the most against the single spell that would kill you. Decide before the fight which spell that is.
check: Which enemy spell is the real threat to you, and where their flankers are.
breaks: If they come from the side instead of the front, your feathers are in the wrong place; walk back toward your team before attacking.

say: Poke with long Paddle Stars and look for one sleep into a kill, or farm and keep distance if they have someone who dives.
more: Paddle Star deals more the further it flies in a straight line, so your damage comes from distance and angle, not from standing close.
A sleeping target takes doubled damage from the first hit that wakes them, up to a cap. One bubble into one long star can remove a carry.
You are fragile and your only movement is a jump that returns you. You win before fights start, not in the middle of them.
check: Whether there is room for a long, straight shot, and who on their team can reach you.
breaks: If the fight has already started on top of you, stop fishing for the perfect shot; back away and throw what you can from range.

asks: what do I do at six on Zoe
how do I use Portal Jump
can I kill them at six
say: At six, throw Paddle Star backward, jump forward and redirect it for a longer flight, or keep Portal Jump to dodge if they're the threat.
more: Portal Jump blinks you to a nearby spot for one second and then back. It adds distance to the star's path without moving you for good.
Because you always return, it never gets you out. It can sidestep a spell, but you land where you started.
Your first finished item makes a full star on a sleeping target lethal to squishy champions, so the lane changes again there.
check: Where you will reappear after the jump, and whether an enemy is waiting at that spot.
breaks: If their jungler is nearby, do not jump forward for damage; you come back to the same place with your jump spent.

asks: how do I trade on Zoe
how do I poke as Zoe
say: Send Paddle Star behind you first, then redirect it at them for the long flight, or land the bubble first so the star can't miss.
more: The star's damage grows with straight-line distance, so the first cast goes away from the target and the redirect covers the whole length.
After any spell, your next basic attack deals bonus magic damage. Weave an attack in whenever they are close enough.
The bubble makes them drowsy before they sleep. Step back during the drowsy part and line up the long star for the moment they drop.
check: Whether minions are in the star's path, and whether the target is drowsy or already asleep.
breaks: If the wave blocks every angle, do not waste mana on short stars; push the wave with them and wait for a clear line.

asks: what are the things on the ground
should I pick up the drops
how do I use Zoe W
say: Pick up the remnants enemies leave when they use summoner spells or items and cast them yourself, or leave them if grabbing means walking into danger.
more: Spell Thief lets you cast a picked-up summoner spell or item active once. A dropped Flash is an extra escape; a dropped Ignite is extra kill pressure.
Casting any summoner spell also fires three missiles at the nearest target, so even a defensive pickup adds damage.
It is a bonus, not a plan. The lane is still decided by stars and bubbles.
check: What the remnant actually is before you walk to it, and whether it lies inside their range.
breaks: If the remnant is deep in their side of the lane, it is bait whether they meant it or not; let it go.

asks: what do I do before dragon on Zoe
how do I set up objectives as Zoe
where do I stand before the fight
say: Get there early and fish for one sleep from out of sight, then land the star, or just poke and back off if they have divers.
more: One carry removed or sent home before the objective starts usually decides it. That is the whole value you bring to setups.
Standing where they cannot see you makes the bubble far harder to dodge. Arriving first, with dragon on a five minute timer, gives you that spot.
If nothing lands, repeated long stars still take health off whoever walks in, and your team starts the fight ahead.
check: Whether your team has vision around the pit, and where their flankers might come from.
breaks: If the fight starts before you land anything, stay at the back; throw the bubble at whoever dives your team instead of at the far carry.

asks: can I gank side lanes as Zoe
say: Shove, then walk to a side lane and bubble from where they can't see you, or stay and farm if your wave isn't crashing.
more: A bubble from an unseen angle gives the side lane a sleeping target. With the doubled first hit, your star plus their damage is often a kill.
You do not need to walk all the way in. Throwing from river range keeps you safe if it misses.
Leaving on a crashing wave matters more for you than most, because a big wave left under your tower costs you minions and tower health.
check: How far up the side-lane enemies are, and whether their mid laner follows you.
breaks: If the bubble misses, the roam is over; do not walk in to salvage it, go back and catch your wave.
